text:
devon: Heads up — after the control plane upgrade to 1.28 in us-west-2, gpu nodepools stop scaling on demand. We've got multiple pending GPU pods and CA isn't provisioning new GPU nodes. Anyone else seeing this?

simon: Noted. Any CA logs or node labels you can paste?

devon: Pasting a snippet from cluster-autoscaler logs and kubectl outputs. CA keeps saying it can't find a nodegroup for the GPU nodes.

devon: ```
I1119 16:02:12.345678 1 scale_down.go:123] Node group not found for node "ip-10-0-45-87.us-west-2.compute.internal" - ignoring
I1119 16:02:12.345690 1 utils.go:98] No node group discovered for node with labels: map[topology.kubernetes.io/zone:us-west-2a topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type:p4d.24xlarge alpha.kubernetes.io/nvidia-gpu:present]

kubectl get nodes -L node.kubernetes.io/instance-type,topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type,node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu
NAME                                    STATUS   ROLES    AGE   LABELS
ip-10-0-45-87.us-west-2.compute.internal   Ready    gpu     8d   topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type=p4d.24xlarge,node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=
```

maria: Hmm — note CA log shows it expects node.kubernetes.io/instance-type but node only has topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type. During the 1.28 kubelet/cloud-provider update we switched to topology labels and apparently our autoscaler discovery was only matching the older node label key.

jess-oncall: That would explain why CA can't map nodes to ASG node groups. Pending GPU pods are piling up in prod-ml. Cost impact: 40 pending pods on several customers with larger batch jobs stuck.

infra-bot: [alert] 1799991200 - PendingPodSpike in cluster-prod-usw2: 40 pending GPU pods > 10m

simon: Quick mitigation — we can update the CA deployment args to accept both label keys (if using regex/auto-discovery flags) or roll a tiny sidecar that re-adds the legacy label to nodes. Which is faster?

maria: Patch to CA config is safer long-term but requires a rollout and validation. Fastest immediate workaround: daemonset that adds node.kubernetes.io/instance-type based on topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type. I've done this before.

devon: Example daemonset (quick and dirty) — it just runs kubectl label on the node when the pod starts:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: copy-instance-type-label
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: copy-label
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: copy-label
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: node-labeler
      hostPID: true
      containers:
      - name: labeler
        image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c"]
        args:
          - node=$(cat /etc/hostname) && \
            val=$(kubectl get node $node -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels["topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type"]}') && \
            kubectl label node $node node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=$val --overwrite
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount
          name: kube-token
      volumes:
      - name: kube-token
        projected:
          sources:
            - serviceAccountToken:
                path: token
                expirationSeconds: 3600
```

jess-oncall: Create ServiceAccount node-labeler in kube-system with clusterrolebinding to allow node/patch. Do it in a limited-scope way (only nodes & only label patch).

simon: I'll prepare the CA config change too — set auto-discovery flags to accept label keys: --node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled=true and add --node-group-auto-discovery=label=topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type OR update CA pod to run with --node-instance-type-label=topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type (depends on CA version). Which CA version are we on?

devon: We're on cluster-autoscaler v1.28.0. I checked the code — there's a flag --node-instance-type-label but it defaults to node.kubernetes.io/instance-type. We can set it to a comma-separated list? I couldn't find multi-key support in our version.

maria: If CA doesn't support multiple keys, plan A = deploy daemonset to add legacy labels, plan B = upgrade CA to a build that supports new label or patch CA to read alternate label. Also schedule a kubelet/cloud-provider config to set both labels on new nodes going forward.

jess-oncall: Action items:
- simon: deploy the daemonset (proceed with least privilege SA) — target within 10m
- simon: open PR to add node-instance-type-label flag to our CA helm values and test in staging
- devon: monitor pending pods and attach alert suppression while we mitigate (don't spam customers)
- maria: prepare kubelet/cloud-provider config change for the node bootstrap so new nodes get both labels

simon: Deployed the daemonset and RBAC. Patch applied to prod-usw2. Verifying CA logs now.

simon: CA log snippet after labeler ran: 
```
I1119 16:14:23.987654 1 auto_discovery.go:83] Discovered node group "gpu-pool-1" for node ip-10-0-45-87 (instance-type p4d.24xlarge)
I1119 16:14:24.012345 1 scale_up.go:66] Scaling up group gpu-pool-1: +1 -> 5 desired
```

devon: Pods are draining from pending to scheduling. throughput looks back to normal for the jobs that were queued. Nice.

jess-oncall: Next steps: schedule CA upgrade to a version with explicit support for topology label or submit a small patch to our CA fork to try both keys in discovery. Also add e2e test for node label discovery in our upgrade gating job.

maria: I'll add a test in upgrade-gate showing a node with only topology.kubernetes.io/instance-type and verifying autoscaler finds the group.

simon: Cost note — because scale up was delayed some customers retried workloads and we spiked ephemeral cost by ~8% during the requeues. We'll add a telemetry alert for long PendingGPU time to catch regressions earlier.

devon: Filing incident ticket with timeline and linking the PRs: https://git.redwood.local/infra/ca-fixes/pulls/142 (WIP)

infra-bot: [incident] 1799992000 - GPU Autoscaler discovery incident opened by devon. Priority: P2

jess-oncall: Good work team. Keep the daemonset as a short-term shim. We'll close incident after CA is upgraded and kubelet bootstrap sets both labels.

devon: Will follow up with postmortem draft once we have timestamps and cost impact numbers.
